component.name: Ferret
component.summary: Find and change values in your games

description.p: Health, gold, ammo: pick the number in the game’s window, play a little, and Ferret finds where the game keeps it. Then set it, keep it from going down, and get it back automatically every time you play. A memory editor in the family of Cheat Engine and GameConqueror, made so you don’t need to know what a memory scan is.

ul.li: Click the number in the picture of the game window, or drag a box around it, around a health bar or a row of hearts
Press Start and play: the bar at the top says when it’s your turn to change the number
Save it with a name: Ferret finds it again after the game restarts
Set it, or keep it in a range while you play, with a hotkey to turn that off and on
Browse by name in Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Java, Python, Adobe AIR and Lua games: the character’s numbers listed by the names the game gives them, no search needed
Flip on/off flags in Unreal Engine, Unity and RPG Maker games: the character’s “can be damaged”, the game’s own flags, an RPG Maker game’s switches
One-click tweaks: god mode and fly in Unreal Engine games; god mode, walk through walls, no random battles and walk faster in RPG Maker games
Export your values to a file, or share them with other players and use theirs

description.p: Single-player only: Ferret refuses games with anti-cheat running, online-only games and games that flag edited characters online, and warns about games with online features.
Ferret reads and changes the memory of games you run, so a small helper of its own runs outside the Flatpak sandbox, as you (never as root).

screenshot.caption: Following SuperTux’s coin count: the player’s turn to change it
The coins saved, set to 999 and kept there

description.p: Ferret now updates itself, on Linux through its own Flatpak repository and on Windows with its new installer.
